question.text: If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>p</mi><mo>:</mo></math> "<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn></math> is an odd number" and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>q</mi><mo>:</mo></math> "<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>4</mn><mn>3</mn></msup></math> is an even number" are two statements, then which of the following statements is equivalent to <math><mo>∼</mo><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⇒</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow></mfenced></math>?

options.text: "<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn></math> is an odd number and <math><msup><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></math> is an even number"

The negation of the statement "<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn></math> is not an odd number  or <math><msup><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></math> is not an even number"

Both ("<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn></math> is an odd number and <math><msup><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></math> is an even number") and (The negation of the statement "<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn></math> is not an odd number or <math><msup><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></math> is not an even number")

"<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn></math> is an odd number and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>4</mn><mn>3</mn></msup></math> is not an even number"

solution.text:
∼(p⇒q)≡∼∼p∨q≡p∧ ∼q

Hence, the equivalent statement of ∼p⇒q is ''4 is an odd number and 43 is not an even number''
